report.tagline: A Bengaluru-born auto and cab booking app where drivers pay a small daily fee instead of a commission, built on India's open ONDC network.
report.simpleSummary: Namma Yatri ('our journey' in Kannada) is an app to book autos and cabs, started in Bengaluru in 2022. Drivers do not give a cut of each fare to the app. They pay a flat fee, about ₹25 a day for autos, and keep everything else. Riders pay the meter-style fare directly to the driver. Its code is open source and it runs on ONDC, a government-backed open network, and its model pushed Uber, Ola and Rapido to copy driver subscriptions.

overview.whatItDoes: Namma Yatri connects riders with auto-rickshaw and cab drivers in more than 15 Indian cities, starting with Bengaluru, Chennai, Kolkata and Delhi NCR. It was built by the payments company Juspay and spun out as Moving Tech Innovations in 2023, led by CEO Magizhan Selvan and COO Shanmugavel M.S. It plans to take its open mobility model to Europe.
howItWorks: A rider requests a ride and sees an estimated fare close to the official meter rate.
Nearby drivers see the request and can accept; in some cities they can add a small tip-style top-up.
The rider pays the driver directly by UPI or cash; Namma Yatri takes nothing from the fare.
Drivers pay Namma Yatri a daily subscription, like ₹25 a day, or a small per-ride fee capped after 10 rides.
The app runs on ONDC (Open Network for Digital Commerce), so other apps on the network can show its drivers to their users.
Its code is open source, so anyone can see how matching and pricing work.
overview.valueProposition: Drivers keep 100% of the fare for a tiny daily fee, and riders get fair, transparent prices without surge games.

businessModel.summary: Namma Yatri earns from driver subscription fees, not from fares. It keeps costs low by not handling payments, spending little on marketing and using open source tech.

revenueStreams.detail: About ₹25 a day for autos; cab plans cost more.
₹3.5 per ride for the first 10 rides each day, then free.
Offering its open mobility stack to other cities and countries, such as in Europe.

businessModel.pricing: Free for riders. Drivers pay about ₹25 a day for autos, or ₹3.5 per ride for the first 10 rides. Cab plans vary by city.
businessModel.unitEconomics: A driver doing 15 rides a day at about ₹150 each earns ₹2,250 and pays Namma Yatri ₹25, about 1% of fares. Uber or Ola might take ₹400 to ₹600 of that. Namma Yatri's cost per ride is very low, since it does not move money or fund big discounts. It makes a profit per ride in three of its five main states, but total revenue is still small and the company is not yet break-even.

howTheyGetUsers: Driver word of mouth at auto stands
Public goodwill from its fair-fare story
whatBringsUsersBack: Drivers who accept rides more willingly
growth.moat: Namma Yatri's code is open, so its moat is not technology. It is driver trust and community: drivers in Bengaluru see it as their app. Its low-cost structure lets it survive on fees that would not cover the costs of a heavier company.

competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Uber has better app polish; Namma Yatri has lower driver fees.

competitors.name: Ola
competitors.positioning: Indian incumbent that also moved to driver subscriptions.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Namma Yatri has stronger driver goodwill and transparency.

competitors.name: Government-backed driver apps

pmLessons: A business model can be the product. Namma Yatri's zero-commission plan was its main feature.
Open source and open networks can lower cost and build trust, but they do not give a moat by themselves.
Start with one side of a marketplace. Namma Yatri won drivers first, then riders followed.
Small players can change an industry. Uber and Ola copied driver subscriptions.

interviewQuestions.question: How can Namma Yatri compete when Uber and Ola copy its model?
interviewQuestions.hint: Find what it has that is hard to copy: driver trust, low cost, openness. Pick a focus like small cities.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you fix peak-hour shortages?
interviewQuestions.hint: Diagnose: not enough drivers, low incentives, routes. Ideas: rider top-ups, scheduled rides. Track fulfilment rate.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Namma Yatri raise the driver fee to fund growth?
interviewQuestions.hint: Weigh revenue vs driver trust. Suggest tiered fees or new revenue sources. Guardrail: driver retention.

interviewQuestions.question: How does ONDC help Namma Yatri?
interviewQuestions.hint: Explain open networks, cheaper demand from other apps, and limits. Measure rides from ONDC partners.

interviewQuestions.question: Pick a north star metric.
interviewQuestions.hint: Completed rides per day. Break into drivers, riders, fulfilment and expansion.
